put.description:
Updates an existing journal entry and replaces its line items.

**Amounts.** Send the line amounts as `currency_debit` / `currency_credit`, in the journal's currency. The base-currency `debit` / `credit` fields are derived by the server (`currency_* x currency_rate`) and anything sent in them is overwritten - a payload that carries only `debit` / `credit` has every line discarded and is rejected with `400`.

**Line items are a full replacement.** The `JournalTransaction` array is the complete set: a line with `id` updates that line, a line without `id` is inserted, and any existing line missing from the array is deleted. A line `id` that belongs to a different journal is rejected with `400`.

**Balance.** The sum of `currency_debit` must equal the sum of `currency_credit`; `total_debit` and `total_credit` on the journal are recomputed from the lines and cannot be set directly.

The `{id}` in the URL identifies the journal. `Journal.id` in the body is optional, but when present it must match the URL id.

post.description:
Create a journal category — a folder in the chart of accounts that groups other categories and posting accounts.

This endpoint creates **categories only**. To create a posting account that journal entries can be booked to, use *Add New Journal Account* instead; an `account_type` sent in this request is ignored.

**Required:** `code` and `name`.

`code` must be **numeric**, and it must not already be used by another category **or** by a journal account — codes are shared across both. Use *GET All Journal Cats* and *GET All Journal Accounts* to find a free code; by convention a child's code extends its parent's (a child of `5` is numbered `51`, `52`, …).

> **A code that is already in use does not return an error.** The request answers with `302` and a `Location` header pointing at the chart-of-accounts page, and no JSON body — so check that the code is free before posting, and configure your client not to follow redirects for this call.

Omit `journal_cat_id` to create a top-level category, or set it to the reference of the parent category to nest this one beneath it.

Only the `JournalCat` object is read from the request body; any other top-level object is ignored. `Content-Type` must be `application/json`; another content type, or a body that is not valid JSON, returns `500`.

> **Do not send `id` when creating.** If it holds the reference of an existing category, that category is overwritten instead of a new one being created. Use the *Edit Journal Cats* endpoint to change an existing category.

Requires the *Manage Journal Accounts* permission.

On success the endpoint responds with `202 Accepted` and the reference of the new category.

put.description:
Update an existing expense.

This is a partial update — send only the `Expense` fields you want to change. Any field validated on create keeps its rule when supplied (e.g. a supplied `amount` must be non-zero, a supplied `date` must fall in an open period). The expense id is taken from the path; any `id` in the body is ignored.

Optionally include `JournalTransaction` / `CostCenterTransaction` arrays to replace the account and cost-center allocation, or a `RecurringExpense` object.

The same operation is also reachable via `POST /expenses/{id}`.

An expense that is locked to another record (e.g. generated from another entity) or already used in an expense-distribution transaction cannot be edited.

**Access:** requires the account owner, or staff with *Edit/Delete All Expenses*, or *Edit/Delete His Own Expenses* (for their own records), or *Draft* (for their own draft records).
